AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why do we cover a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. To stop it from rotting
   B. To make it heavier
   C. To keep off rain and sun
   D. To hide it from animals only

2. Where is the best place to make a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. In a very windy open road
   B. In the middle of a stream
   C. A shady, well-drained place near the garden
   D. Inside the kitchen

3. About how long does compost usually take to be ready? (1 mark)
   A. Two years
   B. Ten minutes
   C. One day
   D. Two to three months

4. Why should you wear gloves when handling compost materials? (1 mark)
   A. To make the compost sweeter
   B. To protect your hands from dirt and germs
   C. To keep your hands cold
   D. So the heap grows faster

5. Which pupil is saving water? (1 mark)
   A. One who pours buckets over the whole bed
   B. One who waters with a drip bottle beside each plant
   C. One who waters at midday
   D. One who leaves the tap running

6. What is a good first step if a person's clothes catch fire? (1 mark)
   A. Run fast
   B. Stop, drop and roll on the ground
   C. Jump in the air
   D. Wave the arms

7. Which of these is a fuel used at home for cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Sand
   B. Glass
   C. Cloth
   D. Charcoal

8. Where should kerosene be stored? (1 mark)
   A. In an open bowl
   B. In a labelled container with a tight cap, away from children and fire
   C. Near the fire
   D. In a water bottle on the table

9. Why are tins with pebbles tied on a scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. They feed birds
   B. They make it heavy
   C. They make noise and flash to frighten animals
   D. They store water

10. Which of these is a small wild animal that can destroy crops? (1 mark)
   A. Hen
   B. Goat
   C. Cow
   D. Weaver bird

11. What is poaching? (1 mark)
   A. Feeding wild animals
   B. Watering crops
   C. Illegal killing or capturing of wild animals
   D. Planting trees

12. Which animal often picks maize cobs and bananas? (1 mark)
   A. Hen
   B. Duck
   C. Monkey
   D. Cow

13. Why is it wrong to kill every bird that visits a field? (1 mark)
   A. Birds are always good
   B. Birds also eat harmful insects and are part of nature
   C. Birds pay tax
   D. Birds cannot eat crops

14. Which person is protecting wildlife? (1 mark)
   A. A person who poisons birds
   B. A person who burns a forest
   C. A learner who reports poaching to a wildlife officer
   D. A hunter who sets a trap

15. How do you know millet is ready to harvest? (1 mark)
   A. The plant flowers
   B. The seeds are wet
   C. The plants are green and soft
   D. The heads turn brown and the grains are hard

16. What is a drill in sowing? (1 mark)
   A. A type of seed
   B. A weed
   C. A shallow line in the soil where seeds are sown
   D. A power tool

17. Which site is suitable for planting a fruit tree? (1 mark)
   A. A sunny place with space to spread
   B. Inside a building
   C. A deep shade under big trees
   D. A flooded area

18. Why should you avoid climbing thin branches while harvesting? (1 mark)
   A. They can break and you may fall
   B. They are too sweet
   C. They are cold
   D. They are too high

19. Which of these fruits grows on a woody tree? (1 mark)
   A. Blackberry
   B. Passion fruit
   C. Grapes
   D. Mango

20. Which sign shows a purple passion fruit is ripe? (1 mark)
   A. Deep purple skin that begins to wrinkle
   B. Hard green skin
   C. Bright green skin
   D. A white flower

21. Which nutrient in eggs helps the body to grow? (1 mark)
   A. Salt
   B. Protein
   C. Starch only
   D. Sugar only

22. What does proportion mean in a meal? (1 mark)
   A. The right amount of each kind of food
   B. The number of plates
   C. The colour of the food
   D. The price of the food

23. Which is an advantage of boiling? (1 mark)
   A. It needs deep oil
   B. It needs no oil
   C. It always burns food
   D. It makes food black

24. What is boiling? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking in a little oil
   B. Cooking in the sun
   C. Cooking food in bubbling hot water
   D. Cooking without heat

25. Why are eggs put in cold water after boiling? (1 mark)
   A. To cool them so they are easy to peel
   B. To colour them
   C. To make them raw again
   D. To make them larger

26. Which food is usually shallow fried? (1 mark)
   A. Boiled maize
   B. Tea
   C. Eggs
   D. Boiled rice

27. How often should you brush your teeth? (1 mark)
   A. Once a year
   B. Twice a day
   C. Once a month
   D. Never

28. What is personal hygiene? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking food
   B. Cleaning the compound
   C. Washing cars
   D. Keeping our own bodies clean to stay healthy

29. What should you use to brush your teeth? (1 mark)
   A. A toothbrush and toothpaste
   B. A comb
   C. A knife
   D. A cloth soaked in oil

30. What should you use to wash your hands? (1 mark)
   A. Soap and clean water
   B. Mud
   C. Only dry cloth
   D. Dirty water

31. What is the use of a hygiene log? (1 mark)
   A. Listing games
   B. Measuring rain
   C. Counting money
   D. Recording daily hygiene practices

32. Which is a method of cleaning the home? (1 mark)
   A. Planting
   B. Grafting
   C. Sowing
   D. Mopping

33. Why do we sweep before mopping? (1 mark)
   A. To waste time
   B. To remove loose dirt so it does not turn to mud
   C. Because mops cannot touch water
   D. To use more soap

34. What should you do if your PPE is damaged? (1 mark)
   A. Hide it
   B. Keep using it
   C. Throw it in a river
   D. Tell a teacher or an adult

35. Where should canvas shoes be dried? (1 mark)
   A. In an airy, shady place
   B. Under wet clothes
   C. In a fire
   D. In a sealed box

36. What do you use to scrub gumboots? (1 mark)
   A. A hammer
   B. A soft brush with soapy water
   C. A knife
   D. A heavy stone

37. Which is a correct step for cleaning gloves? (1 mark)
   A. Put them on again dirty
   B. Wear them wet
   C. Snatch them off by the fingers
   D. Pull them off from the wrist so the dirty outside does not touch skin

38. How do you place pins for tacking? (1 mark)
   A. Along the line
   B. Not at all
   C. Only at the edge
   D. Across the line

39. Which item can be made with tacking stitches in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. A car
   B. A house
   C. A handkerchief
   D. A roof

40. What do you use to mark a straight line on cloth? (1 mark)
   A. A broom
   B. Chalk and a ruler
   C. A plate
   D. A hammer

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. What is meant by coexisting with wild animals? (2 marks)

42. Why is poison or a trap not a good way of dealing with wild animals? (4 marks)

43. Describe how to make a tippy tap. (4 marks)

44. State the difference between boiling and shallow frying. (2 marks)

45. Give three uses of chickens. (3 marks)

46. Plan a balanced supper using local foods and name the group of each food. (3 marks)

47. Explain how to make a meal of boiled potatoes and fried egg balanced. (3 marks)

48. Explain what a fruit is in plant growth. (2 marks)

49. Describe how to prepare a class talk about one domestic animal. (4 marks)

50. Explain the difference between domestic and wild animals. (2 marks)

51. Give three ways of saving fuel when cooking. (3 marks)

52. Explain the difference between green and brown materials for compost, with an example of each. (3 marks)

53. Describe how to mop a floor. (4 marks)

54. Sila has a millet field where birds eat the grain every morning. Suggest and explain a plan to protect the crop without killing the birds. (5 marks)

55. Explain three mistakes to avoid when tacking. (3 marks)

56. Name two types of tacking stitches and describe each. (3 marks)

57. List three materials that can be used to make a scarecrow. (3 marks)

58. List three safety rules when harvesting fruit. (3 marks)

59. Describe how to shallow fry an egg. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #4 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — To keep off rain and sun
   A cover protects the heap from too much rain and drying sun.

2. C — A shady, well-drained place near the garden
   A shaded, dry spot protects the heap from sun and flooding.

3. D — Two to three months
   It depends on weather and materials but is usually two to three months.

4. B — To protect your hands from dirt and germs
   Gloves protect against germs and cuts.

5. B — One who waters with a drip bottle beside each plant
   Drip watering is the most water-saving.

6. B — Stop, drop and roll on the ground
   Rolling smothers the flames.

7. D — Charcoal
   Charcoal is burnt to give heat.

8. B — In a labelled container with a tight cap, away from children and fire
   Kerosene catches fire easily and is poisonous.

9. C — They make noise and flash to frighten animals
   Noise and movement scare animals.

10. D — Weaver bird
   Weaver birds and other birds eat grain crops.

11. C — Illegal killing or capturing of wild animals
   Poaching is against the law.

12. C — Monkey
   Monkeys pick crops from farms near forests.

13. B — Birds also eat harmful insects and are part of nature
   Wild animals are needed for balance in nature.

14. C — A learner who reports poaching to a wildlife officer
   Reporting poaching helps protect animals.

15. D — The heads turn brown and the grains are hard
   Ripe grain is hard and dry.

16. C — A shallow line in the soil where seeds are sown
   A drill is a shallow furrow made with a stick.

17. A — A sunny place with space to spread
   Fruit trees need light and space.

18. A — They can break and you may fall
   Safety while picking fruit.

19. D — Mango
   Mango grows on a woody tree.

20. A — Deep purple skin that begins to wrinkle
   Purple types change colour when ripe.

21. B — Protein
   Eggs are body-building foods.

22. A — The right amount of each kind of food
   Proportion means the right amounts.

23. B — It needs no oil
   Boiled food is low in fat.

24. C — Cooking food in bubbling hot water
   Boiling uses hot water.

25. A — To cool them so they are easy to peel
   Cold water stops cooking and cools the eggs.

26. C — Eggs
   Eggs are commonly fried in a pan.

27. B — Twice a day
   Morning and before bed.

28. D — Keeping our own bodies clean to stay healthy
   Personal hygiene is care of the body.

29. A — A toothbrush and toothpaste
   These clean teeth safely.

30. A — Soap and clean water
   Soap removes germs.

31. D — Recording daily hygiene practices
   A log helps to form habits.

32. D — Mopping
   Mopping cleans floors.

33. B — To remove loose dirt so it does not turn to mud
   Mopping dirt makes mud.

34. D — Tell a teacher or an adult
   Damaged PPE may not protect you.

35. A — In an airy, shady place
   Gentle drying protects the shoes.

36. B — A soft brush with soapy water
   A soft brush avoids damage.

37. D — Pull them off from the wrist so the dirty outside does not touch skin
   This prevents germs touching the skin.

38. D — Across the line
   Pins across the line hold the layers.

39. C — A handkerchief
   A handkerchief is an easy first item.

40. B — Chalk and a ruler
   Chalk marks show the line.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Living together peacefully so that both farmers and animals are safe.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for living together, 1 mark for both safe.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: It can kill other animals, pets and people, it hurts animals, and it harms nature.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason, up to 4.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Take a clean jerrican; make a small hole near the cap; hang it; tie a string from the cap to a foot lever; place a basin below and hang soap.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Boiling cooks food in bubbling water. Shallow frying cooks food in a thin layer of hot oil in a pan.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct description.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Eggs, meat, manure, feathers and income (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example, rice (energy), fish (body-building), spinach (protective).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each food correctly named and placed.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Potatoes give energy and the egg gives protein. Add vegetables such as spinach or tomato for protective foods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group named.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: The part of a plant that holds the seeds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for part of a plant, 1 mark for holding seeds.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose an animal; collect pictures; list its uses and care; practise speaking clearly; present and answer questions.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: Domestic animals are kept and cared for by people. Wild animals live freely in nature.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct description.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a lid on the pot, cut food small, use dry firewood, put out the fire after cooking, soak beans first, or use an improved jiko (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Green materials are fresh and wet such as fresh grass or peelings. Brown materials are dry such as dry leaves or straw.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for correct examples.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sweep first; fill a bucket with clean soapy water; squeeze the mop; start from the far corner and mop backwards to the door; rinse the mop; leave the floor to dry with a warning.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: Make a scarecrow with tins and shiny strips, place it in the field, move it every few days, and use a net or a noise maker. Avoid poison because it harms other living things.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for scarecrow and moving it, 1 mark for another method, 1 mark for avoiding poison, 1 mark for reason.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Uneven stitches, pulling the thread too tight, using thread the same colour as the cloth, making a hard knot at the end (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each mistake.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Even tacking has equal stitches and gaps; long and short tacking has a long stitch followed by a short stitch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each name and 1 for correct descriptions.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sticks or poles, old clothes, a sack, dry grass, string, tins, old CDs (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct material.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a ladder or picking pole; do not climb thin branches; wash hands and fruit; use both hands (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

59. (4 marks)
   Answer: Crack the egg into a bowl; heat a little oil in the pan; slide the egg in; cook until the white is firm; lift out with a spatula.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.
